source.paraphrase: ES modules load with import statements. require loads a CommonJS module at runtime and keeps the module graph dynamic.

invariants.why: A require call hides the dependency from static analysis, so bundlers and the checker cannot see the edge.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the call with an import statement at the top of the file, or await an import of the module specifier.
invariants.avoid: Calling require through another object still loads a CommonJS module. A renamed local with the same call shape is still this call.

source.paraphrase: ES modules publish values with export statements. Assigning to module.exports or exports keeps the file on the CommonJS export path.

invariants.why: A CommonJS export in an ES module file splits the public surface across two module systems, and importers read a different shape.
invariants.fixHint: Declare the value and export it with an export statement, or list it in one export block.
invariants.avoid: Assigning into module.exports through a helper still publishes a CommonJS export. Adding one property at a time is still this export.
